story_type: helicopter hoist from a cargo ship in twenty-foot swells and gale winds
hook: A 700 foot ship in 25 foot swells. A crewman aboard was hurt.
narration: This seven hundred foot ship was plowing through swells up to twenty-five feet high.
Thirty miles west of Cape Flattery, Washington, a crewman aboard was hurt.
Canadian rescuers in Victoria called the U.S. Coast Guard for help.
A Dolphin helicopter flew out from Port Angeles into winds of up to fifty-three knots.
[short pause] A ship that big keeps moving during a hoist. So the pilot had to match its speed and hold steady over a deck that rose and fell with every swell.
Then the flight mechanic leaned out the door and ran the hoist cable down through the wind.
outcome: And the Dolphin crew got the forty-five year old crewman off that ship.

location_card.place: 30 miles west of Cape Flattery, Washington

title: 700 foot ship in 25 foot swells
description:
On Nov. 15, 2006, a Coast Guard Air Station Port Angeles HH-65 Dolphin crew airlifted an injured crewman from the 700-foot bulk carrier Iolcos Glory, 30 miles west of Cape Flattery, Washington, in winds up to 53 knots and 20 to 25 foot swells.
